To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of dust, and the dust cooling law that it determines, has a strong effect on the cluster wind dynamics, and that this effect is expected to be particularly important for the cluster central regions and for the bimodal case.

the dust cooling law determines the critical line in the cluster mechanical-luminosity (or cluster-mass) versus cluster size plane and that the critical line separates stationary cluster winds (above it) from bimodal cases (below it).
the presence of dust within massive clusters leads to a stationary balance between the dust cooling and the SN heating of the reinserting matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dust radiative cooling of the reinsertion matter and its effects on the hydrodynamics, and not with the formation or destruction of the dust itself.
the dust radiative cooling and its effects in the hydrodynamics and thermodynamics of the matter re-inserted within young massive super stellar clusters.
the thermodynamics of the matter re-inserted within young and very massive clusters, which is a key ingredient of the evolution of massive clusters and their host galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dust radiative cooling has a major role in determining the hydrodynamics and the evolution of the massive clusters, and thus the star formation process therein.

dust is a major factor to be taken into consideration in order to determine the cluster mechanical energy output, and that the presence of dust within massive clusters is a major factor that determines the cluster evolution and the formation of new stars.
massive clusters with M > 105 M⊙ and ages t < 107 yr are expected to have a stationary presence of gas and dust within their volumes and to be able to drive a wind.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermodynamics of the matter re-inserted within massive clusters is strongly affected by the presence of dust, which, in addition, is a major player in regulating the cluster winds.
the dust radiative cooling is the key to the hydrodynamics and the fate of the matter re-inserted within young and dense clusters.
, in massive star-forming clusters, the thermodynamics of the reinsertion process is dominated by dust cooling, and the dust-to-gaseous mass ratio is determined by the SN rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of dust in the reinserted material is a major player in determining the hydrodynamics and evolution of massive clusters.

dust radiative cooling may be the main factor determining whether massive star clusters are able to drive a wind, and thus to escape the baryon retention and the formation of a new generation of stars.

dust radiative cooling has a strong impact on the cluster dynamics and on the cluster wind properties, which in turn may affect the cluster evolution and the formation and properties of massive galaxies.
